transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-05-20
- Time: 11:00 PT / 14:00 ET
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Rajiv (Solutions Eng), Dana (Lumina VP Eng), Priya (Lumina Platform), Carlos (ML Infra)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to understand Lumina's integration surface, throughput latency targets, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment is right. Discussed SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, gateway/proxy patterns, rate limiting/quotas, and observability hooks. Agreed on TCO worksheet and a technical deep dive next week.

Topics: integration SDKs, langchain, llamaindex, gateway sidecar vs proxy, rate limits, observability/tracing, VPC/private deployment, SOC2/KMS

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Alex, I'm the AE on this account. Samira and Rajiv are here from SE. Dana, Priya, Carlos, hi — want to do quick intros?
[00:18] Dana (Lumina): Hey all, Dana Rivera. We're evaluating options to bolt in LLMs across our internal search and customer support flows. Main ask is predictability — latency under 250ms for short queries, and a cap on cost.
[00:33] Priya (Lumina): Hi, Priya, platform lead. We'll own integration and observability, Carlos is our infra guy.
[00:40] Carlos (Lumina): Carlos Mendes, ML infra, mostly focused on KV cache sizing, batching, and data residency stuff.
[00:49] Samira (Redwood SE): Great — quick note on scope. We support hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem). Today we'll surface integration patterns and pros/cons for each.
[01:05] Dana: Good. We're leaning away from fully on-prem unless necessary — compliance is a factor though: data residency in EU and SOC2 + internal KMS requirement.
[01:18] Rajiv (Redwood): Noted. We have KMS integrations and customer-managed key options for Private and Dedicated; hosted can be used with bring-your-own-key in some enterprise plans. We'll share the security pack.
[01:29] Priya: Walk us through the SDK story — we use LangChain and LlamaIndex in a bunch of services. How heavy is the adaptor work?
[01:40] Samira: Good question. We provide official SDKs for Python and Node with first-class LangChain connectors. For LlamaIndex, there are community adapters — we also keep a maintained example repo. Usually it's a small shim: replace the OpenAI client call with our SDK client and set model/model-variant, caching controls, and async streaming.
[02:05] Carlos: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex's index storage? We store indexes in S3; sometimes the prompts blow up token budgets.
[02:16] Samira: We recommend local prefix caching/KV cache for retrieval-augmented generation. Our runtime supports automatic KV cache across requests which reduces recompute for repeated context tokens.
[02:28] Dana: When you say KV cash — sorry — KV cache?
[02:31] Samira: Yeah, KV cache, sorry, not cash. It's the key-value attention cache. It helps with conversational flows and repeated prefixes.
[02:38] Priya: On the gateway/proxy pattern: we have an existing API gateway and prefer a sidecar approach to avoid more hops. Does Redwood support sidecar?
[02:49] Rajiv: We commonly support both. Two patterns we see: 1) Gateway/proxy where your gateway routes to Redwood's hosted endpoint and handles auth/rate-limit enforcement, or 2) sidecar/adapter deployed next to your services — typically used with Private or Dedicated deployments. Sidecar reduces external network hops but requires deployment work.
[03:10] Dana: Latency budget: in prod we want p95 under 250ms for non-streaming short generations. What's realistic for hosted vs dedicated?
[03:22] Samira: For short prompts with small model variants, Hosted p95 can be sub-200ms in our benchmarks in US regions. Dedicated yields lower variance and more predictable tail latency because you get reserved GPUs and can tune batch sizes. Private can be comparable if you provision accordingly. The tradeoff is cost vs predictability.
[03:41] Carlos: How does batching affect latency — we do concurrent QPS spikes of 400 qps during business hours.
[03:49] Rajiv: Continuous batching optimizes throughput but it can introduce a small additional latency (few tens of ms) depending on batching window. With Dedicated you can control batching policy aggressively and use burst capacity. Also prefix/KV caching can reduce effective token compute.
[04:05] Priya: Rate-limits & quotas — we need per-team quotas and token budget reporting. Can we enforce rate-limits at the Redwood side and get token-level billing hooks?
[04:16] Samira: Yes. Per-token cost breakdown, per-route dashboards, and token-level auditing are available. We also support per-API-key quotas and per-customer ACLs in Dedicated/Private. Hosted has API key based rate-limits; enterprise plans enable finer RBAC.
[04:33] Dana: On observability: we use Datadog and OpenTelemetry. What hooks are available?
[04:40] Rajiv: We emit traces and metrics. We support OpenTelemetry export, and you can ingest logs/metrics via our console hooks. We also provide token-level trace IDs you can correlate back to your app traces.
[04:53] Carlos: Want to see examples of the tracing payload; sample spans, latency breakdown per token.
[04:58] Samira: We'll attach a sample tracing payload and a small demo repo showing Datadog instrumentation.
[05:05] Dana: Security — does Hosted satisfy our SOC2 requirement? If not, we may need Dedicated or Private.
[05:12] Alex: Hosted is offered with SOC2 compliance for enterprise tiers; we'll share the SOC2 report. But Dedicated and Private give more control for KMS and VPC.
[05:22] Priya: Any approvals needed for bring-your-own-key?
[05:26] Rajiv: For BYOK we usually do a brief security onboarding call; it can be part of Dedicated/Private engagement.
[05:31] Dana: Let's dig into integration pattern specifics: we use LangChain agents orchestrating calls to indexes; we want to avoid token blowouts and also keep the latency low.
[05:45] Samira: Two recommendations: 1) Use prompt templates with token budgeting and truncation, 2) Use caching on retrievals and limit context size from LlamaIndex before hitting the model. We can also set per-call max_tokens and early_stop heuristics.
[06:05] Priya: Do you have any prebuilt prompt-management or prompt-store?
[06:09] Rajiv: We don't ship a prompt-store productized, but we have examples and recommend integrate with your existing feature store or a simple prompt-template service.
[06:18] Dana: We saw demos of Redwood Optimize — will that help with quantization recommendations and batching config?
[06:25] Samira: Yes. Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and batching windows per workload, and we tie that to quality monitoring so you can catch regressions.
[06:35] Carlos: For Dedicated trial, what metrics will we get? Full traces, token costs, and per-model latency?
[06:43] Alex: We'll provide the same console dashboard — per-route latency, token breakdown, error rates, and tracing hooks. For Dedicated you can increase retention too.
[06:51] Priya: Connectivity: if we go Private in EU, can we run the control plane in Redwood but the workloads in our VPC?
[06:59] Rajiv: Yes — hybrid private deployment. Control plane remote, runtime inside your VPC. On-prem options also exist for fully air-gapped.
[07:07] Dana: Any notes on SLO-driven routing or fallback models? We sometimes want to fall back to cheaper model when latency spikes.
[07:17] Samira: We support policy-based routing: route by latency, cost, or region. You can configure automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained.
[07:28] Carlos: Regarding quotas again, we must be able to throttle noisy internal teams and give them budgets. Can we issue per-team API keys with separate quotas and alerts?
[07:37] Rajiv: Yes — per-key quotas and alerts, plus webhook notifications for quota exhaustion.
[07:43] Dana: Pricing concerns: we have a 1.5M token/month baseline in peak, with spikes; need to compare per-token hosted vs reserved GPU math.
[07:53] Alex: We'll send a TCO worksheet. Initial quick guidance: Hosted eliminates infra ops but has per-token unit economics; Dedicated is more cost-effective at scale but requires commitment. We'll surface examples.
[08:06] Priya: About SDK integration: can you show a code snippet for LangChain usage?
[08:11] Samira: Sure — the snippet in the repo shows replacing the OpenAI client instantiation with RedwoodClient(api_key=...), then LangChain wrapper that sets model="rwd-3b-qual" and stream=false. We'll include a sample LlamaIndex connector too.
[08:29] Carlos: We prefer minimal changes — ideally config-only changes. How mature are the LangChain connectors?
[08:34] Samira: Mature for common flows — retrieval, chat, text gen. For custom agents, small adaptors are common. We have customers who did config-only swaps for search augmentation.
[08:46] Rajiv: Also note we have a gateway sidecar example that translates your internal request schema into Redwood calls and handles retries/fallbacks.
[08:58] Dana: About retries: do you recommend client-side retries or rely on Redwood SDK?
[09:03] Samira: SDK implements idempotency and recommended retry logic; for non-idempotent ops be careful. Also, our service has built-in circuit breaker hooks.
[09:14] Priya: Observability again — sample dashboards are helpful.
[09:17] Alex: We'll share dashboards and a walkthrough recording.
[09:22] Carlos: Any known issues with LlamaIndex embeddings pipeline? We use embeddings to do chunking and re-ranking.
[09:30] Samira: Embeddings are supported; for high throughput you can batch embedding calls or use async embedding endpoints. Also consider hybrid approach: precompute embeddings and use cached vectors for hot docs.
[09:45] Dana: Data retention and logs — we must ensure we can purge logs or have retention policies per environment.
[09:52] Rajiv: Yes, retention is configurable in Dedicated/Private. Hosted enterprise can have configurable retention windows and exportable audit logs.
[10:02] Priya: Is there an integration for our existing SSO via SAML?
[10:06] Alex: SSO/SAML and SCIM user provisioning are supported for enterprise customers.
[10:11] Dana: Let's talk about a pilot: we want to run a 2-week Dedicated trial connected to our EU region with ~2 GPUs to validate latency and cost. What does that look like?
[10:23] Rajiv: We can provision Dedicated reserved capacity for a short-term evaluation — it would be an engineering-assisted setup. We'll instrument with the same dashboards and give you access. We usually do traffic replay or a small synthetic benchmark.
[10:35] Carlos: For bench, we can provide a representative QPS trace and some prompt sets from our RAG pipelines.
[10:41] Samira: Perfect. We'll run benchmarks and share a results sheet.
[10:46] Dana: Who's the primary POC for security? Priya will lead but wants docs.
[10:51] Alex: I'll send the security pack and SOC2 report. Rajiv will take the technical deep dive.
[10:58] Priya: A few smaller questions: 1) Are there per-request metadata fields for tracing? 2) Can we attach customer-id and team-id?
[11:05] Rajiv: Yes, you can include metadata in the request header that appears in traces. We also allow tagging at the API-key level.
[11:12] Carlos: Any rate-limiting strategies recommended for spikes? Token-based leaky bucket?
[11:18] Samira: Leaky-bucket or token-bucket at the gateway layer works. Redwood can enforce per-key quotas server-side plus webhook alerts; recommend combined client and server-side throttling for best user experience.
[11:31] Dana: One concern: LlamaIndex sometimes sends malformed prompts; any linting or preflight checks?
[11:38] Rajiv: We have a lightweight preflight and prompt-size checks you can enable in the SDK to reject or truncate oversized prompts. We'll include that snippet.
[11:48] Priya: How about function calling / tool calling support with our internal tools?
[11:52] Samira: Function-calling (structured output) is supported — you can map responses to your internal tool invocation layer. There are examples with LangChain agents.
[12:02] Dana: Regarding model variants — we sometimes prefer cheaper 3B variants for re-rank and larger 13B for final generation. How seamless is switching?
[12:13] Rajiv: Seamless — same API parameter to set model-variant. We also have rollback and canary features in the console for gradual rollout.
[12:21] Priya: Any examples of automatic fallback by latency policy?
[12:25] Samira: We'll attach a runbook and example policy JSON that shows fallback from rwd-13b to rwd-3b when predicted latency crosses threshold.
[12:36] Carlos: For our logging compliance, we need logs in-house — can we stream audit logs to our S3?
[12:42] Rajiv: Yes, audit logs can be exported to your S3 or to SIEM via webhook.
[12:48] Dana: Stakeholders and timeline: we want a pilot in June and a decision by end of July. Need buy-in from security and infra.
[12:57] Alex: Good. We'll align the deep dive and security call next week.
[13:05] Priya: Budget: we'll review TCO before pilot sign-off.
[13:09] Alex: Understood.
[13:12] (brief crosstalk, some people talk over each other)
[13:22] Revise plan: I'll share an email with links: security pack, TCO sheet, LangChain/LlamaIndex repo, sample tracing payload, and a proposed time for the deep dive.
[13:32] Dana: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[13:35] Carlos: One quick on quotas: can we set different token cost multipliers for teams? e.g., internal infra team charged differently than product?
[13:44] Rajiv: You can assign quotas and cost centers per API key and tag usage; reporting supports cost allocation.
[13:52] Priya: Great.
[13:55] Alex: OK let's recap next steps.
[13:58] Dana: Yes please.
